about.title: About me
about.summary:
I come from the trades, not from a classic computer science path. That shaped how I work: practical, direct, and focused on things that actually run in production. At Bosch I grew into a role where I talk to internal customers, understand their problems, make technical decisions, build the frontend and backend, and bring the tool online.

Most of my professional work is Next.js, React, TypeScript and Prisma, but I also like leaving my comfort zone. Privately I went into Vue and Nuxt and really enjoyed it. I like trying new things, diving deep, and soaking up everything useful on the way.

aiPosition.title: My position on AI
aiPosition.summary:
I am glad I learned programming before AI became normal in development. From 2019 to 2022 I had to learn the basics the hard way: documentation, source code, debugging, and building things step by step. That matters now, because AI can write code quickly, but somebody still has to know if the result is clean, secure, maintainable, and actually useful.

I use AI every day. For building apps, refactoring code, writing scripts, comparing approaches, or understanding new packages, it is a serious speed boost. But the good results come from knowing how to explain the goal, how to guide the tool, and how to review what comes back.

I think the idea that developers lose their value because of AI is bullshit. When programming became easier before, it did not kill software development. It created more software, bigger systems, and more functionality. I believe the same happens now. Good developers become more valuable, because one strong developer can build things today that used to need a much bigger team.

That means understanding what the customer really needs, shaping the idea, making architecture decisions, estimating effort, keeping people informed, and building frontend and backend with Next.js, React, TypeScript and Prisma. I also decided and built much of the technical setup around it myself: GitHub Enterprise with over 126 repositories, CI/CD and deployment flows, RHEL bare-metal servers, NGINX, PM2, MSSQL operations, and the move toward OpenShift/Kubernetes. On the enterprise side I handle Entra ID applications, role-based access, logs, metrics, documentation, LeanIX, service-level agreements and lifecycle topics, with strict attention to European data protection and internal security requirements.
